## Why This Is Asked
Balancing overhead on a modern filesystem affects multi-tenant login latency; a beginner-friendly plan shows practical risk mitigation and safe rollback.

- Btrfs balance basics, -dlimit/-mlimit throttling, balance status
- I/O monitoring with iostat; systemd timers for scheduling

## Code Example
```bash
# Check progress
sudo btrfs balance status /
# Throttle balance run
sudo btrfs balance start -dlimit=4 -mlimit=4 /
# Pause during peak
sudo btrfs balance pause
# Resume after peak
sudo btrfs balance resume
# Schedule (example) via timer/service
sudo systemctl enable balance-lowload.timer
```

## Follow-up Questions

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This tests practical systemd isolation, idempotence, and testability for regular tasks.

## Key Concepts
- systemd timer and service
- RuntimeDirectory and PrivateTmp
- Idempotent scripts with marker files
- Journald-based verification and dry-run testing

## Code Example
```ini
[Unit]
Description=Periodic cleanup service

[Service]
User=cleanup
Group=cleanup
RuntimeDirectory=cleanup
PrivateTmp=true
WorkingDirectory=/var/lib/cleanup
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/cleanup.sh --marker /var/lib/cleanup/.done
Restart=on-failure
RemainAfterExit=yes
```

```ini
[Timer]
OnBootSec=5min
OnUnitActiveSec=1h
Unit=cleanup.service
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you audit this over time?
- What if the cleanup must run as root?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

This question evaluates practical performance engineering skills for NIC interrupt handling in multi-tenant data ingestion workloads. It requires understanding the interplay between kernel networking, IRQ affinity, multiqueue configuration, and per-tenant CPU pinning.

## Key Concepts

- **IRQ Affinity & CPU Isolation**: Direct NIC interrupts to dedicated cores to avoid contention with tenant workloads.
- **NIC Multiqueue, RPS/XPS, & XDP**: Utilize multiple hardware queues and software steering to distribute packet processing.
- **cpuset/cgroups v2**: Enforce per-tenant CPU placement and resource boundaries.
- **Observability**: Use perf, ftrace, bpftrace, and latency histograms for granular visibility.
- **Safe Testing**: Implement staged load testing with automated rollback procedures.

## Code Example

```bash
# Enable IRQ affinity for NIC (eth0) IRQs
for irq in $(cat /proc/interrupts | grep eth0 | awk '{print $1}' | tr -d ':'); do
    echo 2 > /proc/irq/$irq/smp_affinity  # Pin to CPU core 1
done

# Configure RPS for RX distribution across cores 4-7
echo f0 > /sys/class/net/eth0/queues/rx-0/rps_cpus
echo f0 > /sys/class/net/eth0/queues/rx-1/rps_cpus

# Disable irqbalance
systemctl stop irqbalance

# cgroups v2 per-tenant CPU pinning
mkdir -p /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-a
echo 4-7 > /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-a/cpuset.cpus.effective
echo 0 > /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-a/cpuset.mems
echo $(pgrep -f tenant-a-ingestion) > /sys/fs/cgroup/tenant-a/cgroup.procs
```
